start.headline: Hydroelectric Power – Electricity from Flow
start.paragraph: A hydroelectric power plant converts the movement of water into electrical energy

fundamentals.headline: Hydroelectric Power Plant
fundamentals.paragraph1: Hydroelectric power plants are power plants that convert the energy stored in water into electrical energy. Depending on the type and technology, the amount of electricity they can feed into the power grid varies - some are suitable for continuous basic supply, others only supply electricity temporarily. However, through skillful combination, times of low water levels or high peak demands can be managed well.

dam.headline: Dam
dam.paragraph1: The dam is built to dam up the headwater and thus increase the head. However, the water cannot be dammed up indefinitely. The wall must withstand the enormous pressure of the water masses.

generator.headline: Generator
generator.paragraph1: The generator is connected to the turbine via the shaft. In some cases, a gearbox is interposed - similar to a car. This allows the rotational speed to be regulated depending on the amount of water so that the generator always runs in a favorable speed range.

transformator.headline: Transformer
transformator.paragraph1: With the help of transformers, the electricity generated by the generator can be adapted so that it can be fed into the power grid.

underwater.headline: Tailwater
underwater.paragraph1: The tailwater is the water that has flowed from the headwater through the turbine and exits at the bottom of the dam.

turbine.headline: The Turbine
turbine.paragraph1: The turbine is the heart of the power plant. It transfers the energy of the water to the generator. In our simulation it is a Pelton turbine.

waterflow.headline: Water Flow
waterflow.paragraph1: The water flow indicates what volume of water is transported through the cross-section of the pipe to the turbine per period of time. The unit is m³/s. A low water flow can be compensated for by a greater head. This means: a mountain stream with a small amount of water, which, however, has a head of several hundred meters, can possibly generate more electricity than a large amount of water in a river that just overcomes the height difference of a weir.

damheight.headline: Head
damheight.paragraph1: The water contained in the reservoir is called headwater. Most of the time this is a reservoir. The higher the water is dammed, the greater the height difference between the turbine and the headwater. This height difference is called the head, because it determines how much electricity the hydroelectric power plant can generate.

waterinlet.headline: Water Inlet
waterinlet.paragraph1: In reservoirs, the water of rivers and streams is dammed. In the simulation, inflow quantities of 0 to 100,000 cubic meters per hour can be selected, which can be adjusted using the upper slider.
